prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for store NL-01 (store_code), how many units of each product were sold in February 2025 and in March 2025? order_ts holds UTC time: use its UTC date. Return three columns, in this order: product_id, feb_units and mar_units, with 0 when the product sold nothing at NL-01 in that month. Return one row for each product sold at NL-01 in at least one of the two months. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the join type: a product sold only in March has no February row to start from.
A LEFT JOIN keeps every February product but drops the products sold only in March; the join must keep unmatched rows from both months.
starter_sql:
WITH feb AS (SELECT ol.product_id, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id WHERE s.store_code = 'NL-01' AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01' GROUP BY ol.product_id),
mar AS (SELECT ol.product_id, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id WHERE s.store_code = 'NL-01' AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01' GROUP BY ol.product_id)
SELECT COALESCE(f.product_id, m.product_id) AS product_id, COALESCE(f.units, 0) AS feb_units, COALESCE(m.units, 0) AS mar_units
FROM feb f
LEFT JOIN mar m ON m.product_id = f.product_id
why_this_works: FULL OUTER JOIN keeps the products of both months, and COALESCE fills in the product_id and the units of the month with no sales.
